Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Ireland's response with the bat. The Afghan players spread across the field and take their respective positions. Freddie Ogilby and James West are the two Irish openers who walk to the crease. Abdul Aziz has the new ball and is raring to go. West to take the strike. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

A massive task ahead for Ireland - So 316 is the chase for Ireland to pull off a massive upset, and end their journey on a positive. For Afghanistan, a win here will secure their spot in the semis. Which also means that an Afghan win will knock Sri Lanka out of the tournament. And Ireland's win will keep the Islanders afloat and help them advance to the next stage. But, given the way Afghanistan's bowling has performed in unison, unlike their opponents, they would want to get the job done clinically this time around as well. An interesting run chase ahead coming up. Stay tuned.

Afghanistan overwhelms Ireland. Exploits bowling gaps - After a modest 46 for 2 in the Powerplay, Afghanistan tore through the 11-40 over phase, adding 163 for the loss of just one wicket and completely taking the wind out of Ireland’s sails. Ireland’s bowling woes were exposed once again, with the attack overly reliant on Olly Riley and Reuben Wilson. After a bright start from the duo, the rest of the bowlers couldn’t make any impact, allowing Afghanistan to dominate. The breakthrough came only after a historic 188-run partnership, but by then, the damage was done. Faisal Shinozada fell for 163, thanks to Riley who dismissed him, while Wilson also picked up a couple of wickets in his final spell to reduce Afghanistan from 290/2 to 297/6. However, with Mahboob Khan fighting till the end, his 89 off 79 helped Afghanistan cross 300.

Afghan revival through Faisal Shinozada - After being 27/2 and losing both their openers, including the in-form Osman Sadat, Afghanistan were pushed under tremendous pressure to rebuild and resurrect their innings. And that call was answered sincerely by one of the batting spearheads, Faisal Shinozada who formed crucial alliances first with Uzairullah Niazai and then a marathon partnership with skipper Mahboob Khan. Through these alliances, and Faisal’s sensational century, Afghanistan bossed up that middle phase and made Ireland crave for wickets which never really materialized for them.

Afghanistan inspire in Harare - A sensational batting display from Afghanistan. This is their first 300-plus total this season and an inspiring effort that will be remembered and mentioned for a long, long time. Ireland have been left shellshocked as they just couldn't take wickets at regular intervals to stop this Afghan juggernaut and conceded 106 runs in the last ten overs.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with all the pre-match rituals and it is time for action. The Irish players spread out to their respective fielding positions. Osman Sadat and Khalid Ahmadzai are the two Afghan openers. Reuben Wilson will bowl the first over. Here we go!

Just a few moments away from the game to get underway in Harare. But before that both teams are getting lined up for their national anthems. It will be Ireland's first, followed by that of Afghanistan's.

PITCH REPORT - Melinda Ferrell and HD Ackerman report that there was a touch of morning cloud lingering over Harare. HD says that the match is being played on a brand-new surface, and pitch number four is being used. Says that it is expected to improve as the game progresses. Adds that a few cracks are visible and may widen as the match goes on, the pitch still appears to be a batting paradise.

The captain of Ireland - Olly Riley says that they are happy to bowl first and adds that they will take the positives from the tournament, as they have played good cricket in patches. Mentions that everyone has chipped in and on being asked about who has been the standout for them, Riley thinks about it and credits Luke Murray has been the standout bowler for them this tournament. Informs that they have one change with Alex Armstrong coming in for Bruce Whaley.

The captain of Afghanistan - Mahboob Khan says that the wicket looks pretty good for batting. Mentions that this match is very important for them. Adds that they will try hard to win this and move to the semifinals. Mentions that they have a balanced side and are going with one change, with Aqil Khan coming in for Khatir Stanikzai.

Ireland Under-19 (Playing XI) - James West, Freddie Ogilby (WK), Adam Leckey, Robert O’Brien, Sebastian Dijkstra, Marko Bates, Olly Riley (C), Reuben Wilson, Alex Armstrong (In for Bruce Whaley), Thomas Ford, and Luke Murray.

Afghanistan Under-19 (Playing XI) - Khalid Ahmadzai, Osman Sadat, Faisal Khan, Uzairullah Niazai, Mahboob Khan (C/WK), Aziz Mia Khil, Nooristani, Abdul Aziz, Rohullah Arab, Wahid Zadran, and Aqil Khan (In for Khatir Stanikzai).
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Afghanistan and they have opted to BAT first.

Can Ireland play spoiler in Harare? Pretty much. Ireland have nothing to lose and everything to gain by playing spoilsport to Afghanistan’s semifinal ambitions. But pulling off that shock won’t be straightforward at all. They have lost two of their three chases in this tournament. Afghanistan, meanwhile, have mastered the art of defending totals, winning as many matches by successfully protecting their scores. Let’s hope it’s not a one-sided clash. Toss and teams coming up next.

Ireland’s last hurrah - Ireland’s only win in this tournament came against Japan, but there’s still plenty to be proud of for this spirited squad. They have challenged the heavyweights by displaying that they belong on this stage, even if results haven’t quite gone their way. The batting, though, has been a tale of two men carrying the load - Robert O’Brien and Freddie Ogilby are the lone batters to reach three figures, shouldering the responsibility while their teammates have struggled for consistency. It’s been a similar story with the ball, where the attack has been inconsistent. Reuben Wilson and Olly Riley have led the bowling charge, but the lack of sustained support has made life difficult for the Irish bowlers.

Bowling blitz keeps Afghan dreams alive - It’s no secret that Afghanistan is a bowling factory, churning out talent, and this Under-19 batch proves the production line is running smoother than ever. Leading the charge is the sensational Nooristani, who’s been impressive with a four-wicket haul followed by a five-for in the last game, making him their leading wicket taker. Wahid Zadran and Khatir Stanikzai have been chipping in with crucial breakthroughs as well. Barring that Sri Lanka game, they have bowled out every other opponent. Their victories over South Africa and West Indies, where they successfully defended totals, demonstrate a bowling attack that knows how to handle pressure situations. Batting-wise, their top order has been a consistent one, with openers Osman Sadat and Faisal Khan with a couple of fifties apiece and skipper Mahboob Khan's steady presence as well. And despite their defeat to Sri Lanka in their first Super 6 clash, they are firmly alive and kicking due to such collective efforts.

One semifinal slot, two nervous nations - Dead-rubber, you ask? Not a chance, my friend! This match is as alive as they come. Only the Aussies have stamped their ticket to the semis with that shiny ‘Q’ next to their name, leaving one precious spot for the taking. And what a fight it is! Afghanistan and Sri Lanka are locked in a nail-biting race for the semifinal, while West Indies watch from the sidelines with shattered dreams and Ireland bow out alongside the Proteas. If Afghanistan triumph today, their superior net run rate - sitting pretty in positive territory - will catapult them into second place and straight into the final four. But Sri Lanka, having exhausted their fixtures, are biting their nails and praying for an Irish miracle to dash Afghan hopes and secure their own passage. It’s chess on grass, and we won’t know who joins the Baggy Greens until the very last ball is bowled.

The clash that decides it all - The business end is upon us in the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup, 2026, and the tension is thick enough to cut with a stump! With just a handful of games left in the Super 6 stage, we’ve arrived at the last game of Group 1, a mouth-watering clash between the rampaging Afghanistan and spirited Ireland at the iconic Harare Sports Club. On that note, hello and welcome to the coverage. Buckle up, settle in, and get ready for an exciting ride..

Tournament journeys so far - Hello and welcome to all the fans across the globe. Afghanistan Under-19 and Ireland Under-19 have experienced contrasting fortunes in the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2026. Afghanistan Under-19 advanced to the Super Six stage in strong form, having won all three of their group games against South Africa, West Indies, and Tanzania. They currently sit in second place in Super Six Group 1 with 4 points and a superior net run rate, following a recent loss to Sri Lanka. Ireland Under-19, in contrast, secured only one group-stage victory against Japan and carries no points forward into the Super Six stage, leading to their exit from the tournament. Afghanistan's semi-final push - For Afghanistan Under-19, this match is pivotal for their semi-final aspirations. A victory will solidify their position among the top contenders in Group 1, putting them into a strong position to secure their spot in the knockout stage, given their strong net run rate. Strong performances, including big wins against West Indies and South Africa in the group stage, have marked their campaign. The team, having played warm-up matches in Zimbabwe, is confident in their ability to perform in these conditions. Ireland seeks redemption - Ireland Under-19 enters this match primarily playing for pride and a better tournament finish. With 0 points in the Super Six table and the worst net run rate in their group, the Irish side has already been knocked out of the tournament. They will be looking to finish their campaign on a high note by causing an upset against a strong Afghan side and spoiling the Afghan party. Their previous Super Six match saw them lose to the West Indies by 25 runs (DLS method). The Harare venue and tournament impact - The match is being held at the Harare Sports Club in Harare, Zimbabwe, one of the key venues for the tournament. A win for Afghanistan will likely see them through to the semi-finals, while a win for Ireland would not affect their own standings dramatically but could significantly impact the qualification chances of other teams like Sri Lanka and West Indies, who are close on points to Afghanistan in Group 1. Expect a competitive clash - Expect a highly competitive match, with Afghanistan eager to secure the win needed for a semi-final spot and Ireland keen to end their tournament on a positive note. Afghanistan's strong form and familiarity with the Zimbabwean conditions give them a psychological edge, but Ireland will be determined to fight for a morale-boosting victory. Fans can likely expect an engaging contest as both teams give their all in their final Super Six fixture.
